title: Converge Learn-it Atlas on one learning journey
purpose: Complete the evidence-backed R4 successor correction authorized by issue #352: preserve the single existing Atlas learning journey while replacing large multi-column course cards with compact vertically scannable course rows and progressively disclosing detailed progress and end-of-session evidence. Preserve persisted history, resume, review-needed, lineage, revisions, imports, storage and accessibility behavior.
invariants: Atlas learning actions from Today and Library enter the same existing Atlas planner/session engine; no third runtime or learner mode is introduced.
An active Atlas activity hides Today chrome, the classic Library surface, unrelated Atlas course rows and replanning controls while keeping prompt and answers contiguous.

R4 changes only presentation topology: Today and Library are compact vertically scannable lists, essential Atlas state is visible directly, detailed objective progress uses a full-width disclosure, and summary history is disclosed on demand.
The final activity remains visible with its own feedback and an explicit Voir le bilan action before the summary is rendered.
Atlas event commits, history, resume state, review-needed semantics, package/course/activity lineage, revision IDs/digests and import behavior are unchanged.
No storage schema, database version, migration, backend, account or sync behavior is introduced.
learnit.kit.v2 and all EPF kit payloads remain unchanged.
Keyboard/focus behavior remains based on the existing Atlas controls and focus assertions, with minimum target sizing preserved.
requiredEvidence: PR scope validates exactly against ATLAS-WP-024.
Learn-it Next CI runs the bounded atlas-ux-convergence profile inside the existing workflow on the exact PR head, using only the current build and existing relevant tests.

Existing Atlas integration and UX clarity tests cover Library routing, exclusive active surface, compact course-list topology, Atlas-derived essential progress, full-width collapsed detail, final feedback before Voir le bilan, concise summary detail disclosure and learner-facing import copy.
The deterministic Learn-it Next source manifest is rebound to every changed manifest-owned source.

Before/after evidence is prepared for Today topology, Library topology, collapsed essential progress, expanded full-width detailed progress, final answer plus feedback, Voir le bilan, concise summary plus optional detail and import wording.
No learner usability PASS is declared before the R4 human replay.
adversarialTests: apps/learnit-next/tests/atlas_m1_int.py checks that Atlas Library actions cannot fall through to the classic learning handler, active sessions suppress competing surfaces, and R4 presentation primitives remain wired without changing the runtime.

apps/learnit-next/tests/atlas_m2_ux_clarity.py checks Atlas-derived compact progress, progressive summary disclosure and the final-feedback-to-bilan transition while retaining prior Atlas UX clarity coverage.
nonGoals: Changing EPF kits or the learnit.kit.v2 contract.
Migrating or merging classic and Atlas storage.
Adding backend, accounts, sync, a theory/discovery mode, a third runtime or a broad dashboard redesign.
Adding search, filtering, sorting, new navigation architecture or unrelated visual polish.
Creating a new contradictory-QA chain or declaring human usability PASS.
independentReview: Issue #352 is the sole implementation authority and contains the R4 driver arbitration GO_R4_BOUNDED_COMPACT_COURSE_LIST_PROGRESSIVE_DISCLOSURE.
The accepted Human Replay R3 on 16aa6859ab76fc7ad26e228f1774e2dc6d369e68 is the evidence basis for this bounded successor correction.
A short R4 human replay owns the learner-usability verdict; this implementation stream must not self-certify UX PASS.
rollback: Close or revert PR #354. The baseline storage, contracts, EPF kits and pre-existing Atlas/classic persisted data remain unchanged.
